title: Bounded runs
lesson: A harness-owned call budget ends an unsuccessful run; a passing result can exit to review before that budget is spent.

transcript.text: Run A has a three-call budget. Three agent-to-tool cycles consume it. Amber RETRY results return feedback; they do not mean the task has succeeded.
With no calls remaining, the run routes to Stop. The stage fades to separate this exhausted task from the next example.
An independent run B starts with its own three-call budget. After one continuing result, a second tool result becomes PASS and travels to Review with one call left.
The edit loop dims and Review remains active. The run has ended successfully for review; the animation does not show merge approval. A full-frame fade closes the loop.

limitations: The three-call budget and outcomes are illustrative, not a recommended production limit.
The diagram abstracts the harness implementation and does not show timeout cancellation, evidence classification or a blocker handoff.
The separate run B must be authorized independently; an exhausted agent cannot refill its own budget.

changes: Added orientation title, distinct amber continuing results versus green PASS, a labelled and faded independent-run reset, and Review as the successful endpoint.
Shortened the final hold; capped local renderer FFmpeg threads.
